title: Create Your Offer
lede: Choose one buyer, understand one problem and turn the solution into an offer.
deliverable: One niche, one understood service and one saved offer ready to use on a landing page.
body:
Start with one type of business. Find a problem they want solved. Get clear on the service, then write the offer. You do not need to invent the whole business in one prompt.

1. Choose your niche

Start with an industry you know, have worked in or can reach. If you have no idea yet, tell Jarvis your background and interests and compare a few. Pick one to investigate.

Help me choose one niche from my background and interests, then save my chosen buyer and location.

Check: you can name the business owner you want to help.

2. Find the problem and match a service

Research what goes wrong in that business and why it matters. Then match the problem to a service. The services here are starting points, not a list you must choose from.

Use the offer menu skill to research my chosen niche, recommend one problem worth solving and match it to a service with real examples.

Check: you can explain why the owner would pay to fix it.

3. Understand what you will deliver

Before a promise goes on a page, know what you will build, how it helps and who delivers it. For a custom system, get your developer or technical CSM to check the scope. A demo can show the idea, but it does not prove a result you have never delivered.

Explain my chosen service in plain language: the problem, what we install, how it produces the result, what the client still does and how I will deliver it. Save the brief and flag what needs checking.

Check: you can explain the service to a mate in two sentences.

4. Write the offer

Now write the six lines. The target, timing and guarantee need to fit the service you can deliver.

Use my saved service brief and the offer creation skill to write my six lines.

Check: the result, timing and guarantee match the service you understand. Save the offer; Jarvis uses it to write your landing-page headline and subheadline.

For an audit-led agency, the first offer is the audit. The specific paid build is scoped after you diagnose the business.
